request.spec:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The consolidated figures now follow the new rule, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What now happens:**
- **Due-total and overdue-total:** each person's figure from every sheet in the tree goes into one list. If three or more people have a figure, the single highest and single lowest are dropped once over that whole list. Before, each sheet's already-trimmed total was added up.
- **People count:** each person is counted once across the tree. People whose name or any alias matches, ignoring case (the way the app already compares names), count as one. The matching chains, so if A matches B and B matches C, all three are one person.
- **What goes into the trim:** the same per-sheet inputs as before. Due-totals of "n/a" are left out, and every person's overdue-total goes in.

**One judgement call:** for the trim, a person who appears on two sheets still counts as two separate figures; they are only merged for the people count. The request is ambiguous on this, but the test data needs it: the first test expects 9.00, which comes out only if Ada's two figures (4.00 and 2.00) stay separate. Adding them into one 6.00 would give 7.00.

**Changes** (all front end; no server or stored-data change was needed):
- `features/claims/claims.ts`: `useSheetTotals` also returns the untrimmed per-person due and overdue figures. Its existing totals are unchanged.
- `features/consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx`: each sheet now passes up its people's names and aliases and those per-person figures. The consolidated panel merges people who share a name and trims the due and overdue totals once over the whole tree. The per-grade due-totals and per-status counts are still added up sheet by sheet as before.
